messages:
monitor-bot: ALERT: internal-lb-prod (zone-a) 502 spike -> 1200/min, elevated latency p95=420ms. Affected: service-genesis-east. dashboard: https://grafana.company/internal-lb :rotating_light:

alex: Seeing the same from app-side. Multiple backends reporting connection resets and probe failures. Opening thread to correlate ToR counters.

maria: Quick check: ran an iperf between r2->r3, shows ~0.2% packet loss intermittently. Suspect MTU mismatch after last config push (some devices at 9000, others at 1500).

jordan: Pulled proxy logs, seeing repeated: `recv: invalid checksum` and `SYN retries 3`. Health checks to backend sockets timing out -> 504/502 bubbling up.

alex: From proxy-node-7: `ssh ops@tor14 \"ethtool -k eth0\"` returned GRO: on, GSO: on, TSO: on. `ip link show` on host -> mtu 9000, but ToR reports interface mtu 1500.

maria: Confirmed: last night's edge template change set `mtu: auto` in ansible role. Some ToRs applied 1500, others left as 9000. That explains fragmentation + RDMA fallback weirdness.

jordan: Captured `ss -tin` on proxy-node-7, snippet: ```State      Recv-Q Send-Q Local Address:Port Peer Address:Port 
ESTAB      0      0      10.10.3.7:443        10.10.8.12:52344  
... retrans: 42, out-of-order: 18```

alex: Stopgap: disabled GRO/GSO/TSO on proxy-node-7: `ethtool -K eth0 gro off gso off tso off`. Health probes improved quickly, 502 rate down ~60% in 6m, but CPU on proxy jumped ~12%.

liam: That's a good short-term mitigation but not sustainable at scale. Proposal: 1) reconcile ToR MTU templates to uniform 9000, 2) staged ToR config rollout with rack-level windows, 3) add LB fallback routing to alternate ToR if health probes fail.

maria: Also noticed autoscaler bursts cause many new GPU pods to warm KV caches -> large continuous flows. Those large segments are where fragmentation hits hardest when MTU mismatch exists.

ops-bot: Created INFRA-4823: \"ToR MTU drift causing L4 proxy probe failures and 502 spike\". Owners: eng-infra (maria, alex). Target maintenance window: 2024-12-07 02:00 UTC.

alex: Runbook (short): 
1) revert ansible `mtu: auto` change -> enforce 9000
2) roll ToR updates in groups of 4 racks, verify `ip link` and `ethtool -k` post-change
3) add an MTU probe to LB health check: `ping -M do -s 8972 <backend>` and failover route if fragmentation occurs
4) re-enable GRO/GSO after ToRs reconciled

liam: /cc @oncall for scheduling. Also recommend temporary LB policy: route new sessions to alternate ToR within the same AZ when a rack reports probe failures to avoid cross-AZ perf hit.

maria: I'll draft the step-by-step and post to #eng-infra-runbooks + link the ticket. Thanks all — temp mitigation worked, but need the ToR rollout to close this out :thumbsup:
